## Continuation Wave 21 — Plan 12 — Learning Houses, Oral History, and Civic Teaching

Wave 21 adds a new owner-bound layer for **learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners**. Material anchors include **a story tile with a blue triangle, a bell on a wall hook, a map with a braided loop, and a note held by a tack**. Observable markers include **triangle legibility, hook bell reach, braided loop continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback reach**.

### Pass 221 — Blue Triangle Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners; it does not mint a second learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching ledger. Treat the visible markers triangle legibility, hook bell reach, braided loop continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback reach as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Blue Triangle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees triangle legibility, hook bell reach, braided loop continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback reach with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Blue Triangle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a story tile with a blue triangle, a bell on a wall hook, a map with a braided loop, and a note held by a tack become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Blue Triangle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Blue Triangle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present triangle legibility, hook bell reach, braided loop continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback reach with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Blue Triangle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a story tile with a blue triangle, a bell on a wall hook, a map with a braided loop, and a note held by a tack as physical evidence and triangle legibility, hook bell reach, braided loop continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback reach as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Blue Triangle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Blue Triangle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Blue Triangle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises triangle legibility, hook bell reach, braided loop continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback reach at their boundary values.

**Blue Triangle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Blue Triangle Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 23 — Plan 12 — Learning Houses, Oral History, and Civic Teaching

Wave 23 adds a new owner-bound layer for **learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners**. Material anchors include **a story tile with a violet bar, a bell on a curved hook, a map with a nested route, and a note clipped with wire**. Observable markers include **bar legibility, curved bell reach, nested route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback index**.

### Pass 243 — Violet Bar Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners; it does not mint a second learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching ledger. Treat the visible markers bar legibility, curved bell reach, nested route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback index as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Violet Bar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees bar legibility, curved bell reach, nested route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback index with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Violet Bar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a story tile with a violet bar, a bell on a curved hook, a map with a nested route, and a note clipped with wire become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Violet Bar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Violet Bar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present bar legibility, curved bell reach, nested route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback index with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Violet Bar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a story tile with a violet bar, a bell on a curved hook, a map with a nested route, and a note clipped with wire as physical evidence and bar legibility, curved bell reach, nested route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback index as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Violet Bar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. **Violet Bar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. ## Continuation Wave 24 — Plan 12 — Learning Houses, Oral History, and Civic Teaching

Wave 24 adds a new owner-bound layer for **learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners**. Material anchors include **a story tile with a silver ring, a bell on a split hook, a map with a spiral route, and a note fastened with a clip**. Observable markers include **ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas**.

### Pass 254 — Silver Ring Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners; it does not mint a second learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching ledger. Treat the visible markers ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Silver Ring Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Silver Ring Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a story tile with a silver ring, a bell on a split hook, a map with a spiral route, and a note fastened with a clip become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Silver Ring Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Silver Ring Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Silver Ring Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a story tile with a silver ring, a bell on a split hook, a map with a spiral route, and a note fastened with a clip as physical evidence and ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Silver Ring Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Silver Ring Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Silver Ring Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas at their boundary values.

**Silver Ring Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Silver Ring Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

The proposed extension stays over journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners; it does not mint a second learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching ledger. Treat the visible markers ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Bell Reach Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Bell Reach Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a story tile with a silver ring, a bell on a split hook, a map with a spiral route, and a note fastened with a clip become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Bell Reach Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Bell Reach Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Bell Reach Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a story tile with a silver ring, a bell on a split hook, a map with a spiral route, and a note fastened with a clip as physical evidence and ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Bell Reach Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Bell Reach Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Bell Reach Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas at their boundary values.

**Bell Reach Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Bell Reach Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Learning Atlas Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises ring legibility, split hook reach, spiral route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback atlas at their boundary values.

**Learning Atlas Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. ## Continuation Wave 25 — Plan 12 — Learning Houses, Oral History, and Civic Teaching

Wave 25 adds a new owner-bound layer for **learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners**. Material anchors include **a story tile with a teal bar, a bell on a low bracket, a map with a turning route, and a note clipped to a ring**. Observable markers include **bar legibility, bracket bell reach, turning route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback compass**.

### Pass 265 — Teal Bar Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners; it does not mint a second learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching ledger. Treat the visible markers bar legibility, bracket bell reach, turning route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback compass as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Teal Bar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees bar legibility, bracket bell reach, turning route continuity, consent drift, room welcome, and callback compass with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Teal Bar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a story tile with a teal bar, a bell on a low bracket, a map with a turning route, and a note clipped to a ring become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Teal Bar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. **Teal Bar Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 27 — Plan 12 — Learning Houses, Oral History, and Civic Teaching

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners**. Material anchors include **a slate with a blue half-moon, a cup ring on a reading bench, a thread map stitched in linen, and a token cut from a roof tile**. Observable markers include **half-moon contrast, cup ring age, thread map continuity, token consent, room belonging, and callback route**.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Material anchors include **a book spine patched in hide, a chalk spiral on a beam, a ribbon threaded through a map, and a clay token stamped with a wave**. ### Pass 309 — Hide Spine Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners; it does not mint a second learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching ledger. Treat the visible markers spine tension, spiral legibility, ribbon sequence, wave consent, circle welcome, and callback thread as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Hide Spine Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees spine tension, spiral legibility, ribbon sequence, wave consent, circle welcome, and callback thread with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Hide Spine Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. ## Continuation Wave 30 — Plan 12 — Learning Houses, Oral History, and Civic Teaching

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners**. Material anchors include **a paper star pasted to a wall, a bell cord looped around a peg, a stitched path on canvas, and a clay tab marked with a dot**. Observable markers include **star contrast, cord reach, path stitching, dot consent, room safety, and callback path**.

### Pass 320 — Paper Star Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners; it does not mint a second learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching ledger. Treat the visible markers star contrast, cord reach, path stitching, dot consent, room safety, and callback path as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Paper Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees star contrast, cord reach, path stitching, dot consent, room safety, and callback path with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Paper Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a paper star pasted to a wall, a bell cord looped around a peg, a stitched path on canvas, and a clay tab marked with a dot become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Paper Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Paper Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present star contrast, cord reach, path stitching, dot consent, room safety, and callback path with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Paper Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a paper star pasted to a wall, a bell cord looped around a peg, a stitched path on canvas, and a clay tab marked with a dot as physical evidence and star contrast, cord reach, path stitching, dot consent, room safety, and callback path as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Paper Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Paper Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Paper Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises star contrast, cord reach, path stitching, dot consent, room safety, and callback path at their boundary values.

**Paper Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Paper Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

### Pass 331 — Copper Star Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners; it does not mint a second learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching ledger. #### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees star patina, leaflet fold, thread ring, line consent, room calm, and callback lane with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Copper Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. ## Continuation Wave 32 — Plan 12 — Learning Houses, Oral History, and Civic Teaching

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners**. Material anchors include **a tin star pinned to canvas, a slate triangle beneath a lamp, a cord bridge across a map, and a clay stamp with two bars**. Observable markers include **star shine, triangle clarity, bridge tension, bar consent, room welcome, and callback route**.

### Pass 342 — Tin Star Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over journal, culture, relationship, roster, documentation, archive, scenario, and accessibility owners; it does not mint a second learning houses, oral history, and civic teaching ledger. Treat the visible markers star shine, triangle clarity, bridge tension, bar consent, room welcome, and callback route as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Tin Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees star shine, triangle clarity, bridge tension, bar consent, room welcome, and callback route with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Tin Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a tin star pinned to canvas, a slate triangle beneath a lamp, a cord bridge across a map, and a clay stamp with two bars become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Tin Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Tin Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present star shine, triangle clarity, bridge tension, bar consent, room welcome, and callback route with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Tin Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a tin star pinned to canvas, a slate triangle beneath a lamp, a cord bridge across a map, and a clay stamp with two bars as physical evidence and star shine, triangle clarity, bridge tension, bar consent, room welcome, and callback route as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Tin Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Tin Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Tin Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises star shine, triangle clarity, bridge tension, bar consent, room welcome, and callback route at their boundary values.

**Tin Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Tin Star Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.
